simple.meaning: רַב־סָרִיס (Rab-Çârîyç) is a Hebrew word meaning “Rab-Saris , a Babylonian official.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: רַב־סָרִיס (H7249) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Kings 18:17, with occurrences in 2 Kings, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רַב־סָרִיס (H7249) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in רַב־סָרִיס (H7249) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: רַב־סָרִיס (Rab-Çârîyç) / H7249 is traced through 2 Kings 18:17, Jeremiah 39:3, Jeremiah 39:13 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The king of Assyria sent Tartan and Rabsaris and Rabshakeh from Lachish to king Hezekiah with a great army to Jerusalem. They went up and came to Jerusalem. When they had come up, they came and stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is in the highway of the fuller’s field.

timeline.evidenceText: The king of Assyria sent Tartan and Rabsaris and Rabshakeh from Lachish to king Hezekiah with a great army to Jerusalem. They went up and came to Jerusalem. When they had come up, they came and stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is in the highway of the fuller’s field.

All the princes of the king of Babylon came in, and sat in the middle gate, Nergal Sharezer, Samgarnebo, Sarsechim, Rabsaris, Nergal Sharezer, Rabmag, with all the rest of the princes of the king of Babylon.
So Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard sent, with Nebushazban, Rabsaris, and Nergal Sharezer, Rabmag, and all the chief officers of the king of Babylon;
